newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - WH Smith weighing U.S. options.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - WH Smith weighing U.S. options.

text.p: Britain's leading newsagents group WH Smith Plc on Wednesday said it had not ruled out disposing of its music retailing business in the United States.
"Disposal is certainly an option," WH Smith chief executive Bill Cockburn told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"There are far too many music retailers (in U.S.) and there is going to be a big shakeout," he added.

Operating profits at the company's "Wall' music retail chain in the U.S. dipped to $4.8 million from $7.6 million as a result of aggressive price competition -- competition that Cockburn believes will drive many retailers into bankruptcy.
"A lot of the competition will be filing for Chapter 11 (U.S. bankruptcy protection). Trying to sell the Wall now would not be smart -- there are more sellers than buyers."
The Wall will be retained for now but Cockburn said no further investment would be made in the U.S. retailer until the market prospects became clearer.
"But who knows what might be created out of the wreck (of U.S. market). There may be a new phoenix of an opportunity and we might figure strongly in that," Cockburn said.
Smiths does see a growing opportunity for expansion in U.S. airports, however.
